messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV3 — gpu-node-17 reported a spike in corrected ECC errors (prom alert gpu-ecc-spike) at 2026-03-10T18:00Z. Rule: increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1m]) > 0. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/4321

lucy: I'm on it, paging SRE @ben and platform @maria. Starting quick triage — will check NVSMI and prometheus.

ben: oncall here. looking at prometheus now, huge burst: increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total{node="gpu-node-17"}[5m]) -> 27 in that window. also seeing fan RPM oscillation in the same timeframe.

maria: VRAM temp climbed to ~86C sustained for ~6m, but utilization was low (~12%). odd — could be a fan/power/driver scheduling issue rather than load.

lucy: is this causing customer impact?

joel: small impact — customer-42 reported higher tail latency on embedding endpoints 17:58-18:05. Not mass failure but some requests hit a slow pod on that node.

lucy: plan: 1) cordon + drain node 2) failover critical pods 3) silence noisy alert for this node 4) create follow-up tickets for hardware diag and alert tuning. executing drain now.

lucy: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60``` 

incident-bot: Drain job started for gpu-node-17, 12 pods scheduled to be evicted. ETA ~3m.

ben: drain completed. pods evicted 12/12. node in cordoned state.

ben: recommendation: the current prom rule firing on any corrected ECC increment is way too noisy. propose: make it a 5m window and require >5 corrected ECCs in 5m, i.e. increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m]) > 5. Also add a composite alert that requires VRAM_temp > 85 and ECC spike for >3m to escalate to SEV.

maria: +1. Also surface fan_rpm and driver_version on the gpu health panel. We should gate automatic escalation on temp/fan correlation.

lucy: applying a temporary silence for gpu-node-17 on gpu-ecc-spike and opening PR for rule change. Updating dashboard to include ECC timeseries, VRAM temp, fan RPM, and recent driver pkg. Dashboard link: https://redwood.console/dashboards/gpu-health?node=gpu-node-17

joel: note for runbook: check kernel/driver rollouts in the rack — recent kernel bump could explain new behavior. tagging ops-release for audit.

ben: quick safety note: these are corrected ECCs (no uncorrectable/errors), so immediate data-loss risk low. but corrected ECCs at this rate + thermal oscillation suggests memory instability under some clock/power states — hardware diag recommended.

lucy: handing off long-lived tasks to @ben for postmortem and next steps. I'll annotate timeline and customer impact and create SRE tickets.

ben: follow-ups I'm tracking: - SRE-1234: hardware diag & replace node if needed - SRE-1235: alert tuning (5m window + composite) - SRE-1236: dashboard widgets and synthetic tests - SRE-1237: add driver/kernel correlation check to runbook

maria: I'll search release logs for any recent driver/kernel changes on that rack and post findings in the ticket.

lucy: rationale for alert tuning in the PR: corrected ECCs are noisy on healthy hardware; we need to reduce paging noise while keeping signal for real issues. Change summary: 1) change rule window to 5m and threshold to >5; 2) add composite rule (ECC + VRAM_temp > 85C for 3m) -> SEV; 3) keep low-priority ECC single-sample rule for ops dashboards only.

joel: also proposing a staging synthetic: run mem-stress with varied clock/power states across different drivers to try to reproduce corrected-ECC spike pattern. assigning to infra-team.

ben: creating PR "tune gpu_ecc_spike: 5m window & composite condition" and linking runbook updates.

lucy: status update: node reprovisioned onto new host, no further alarms for last 25m. customer-42 notified with an explanation and mitigation notes. closing pager for now. Handing final ownership to ben for postmortem. please ack.

maria: ack — thanks everyone. :thumbsup: :heart:

incident-bot: Incident closed by lucy. Duration 00:46. Severity downgraded from SEV3 to SEV4 in follow-up. Postmortem ticket SRE-1240 created: https://redwood.internal/sre/tickets/SRE-1240
